/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from math import sqrt, sin, cos, pi
from itertools import combinations

def tr(A): return list(map(list,zip(*A)))
def mm(A,B): return [[sum(a*b for a,b in zip(row,col)) for col in zip(*B)] for row in A]
def sub(A,B): return [[a-b for a,b in zip(ar,br)] for ar,br in zip(A,B)]
def inner(A,B): return sum(a*b for ar,br in zip(A,B) for a,b in zip(ar,br))
def n2(A): return inner(A,A)
a=1/sqrt(2); q=a/2
X=[[0,a,a],[a,0.5,-0.5],[a,-0.5,0.5]]
W=[[0,q,-q],[-q,0,0],[q,0,0]]
S=[[0,1,1],[1,1,-1],[1,-1,1]]
G0=[[v/2 for v in row] for row in mm(W,X)]
A=sub(G0,S)
def F(Y): return inner(A,Y)+sum(abs(v) for row in Y for v in row)
def update(i,j,theta,reflect=False):
 c,s=cos(theta),sin(theta)
 V=[[-c,s],[s,c]] if reflect else [[c,s],[-s,c]]
 Y=[row[:] for row in X]
 Y[i]=[V[0][0]*u+V[0][1]*v for u,v in zip(X[i],X[j])]
 Y[j]=[V[1][0]*u+V[1][1]*v for u,v in zip(X[i],X[j])]
 return Y
print('X =',X)
print('A =',A)
print('Orthogonality residual squared:', n2(sub(mm(tr(X),X),[[1,0,0],[0,1,0],[0,0,1]])))
print('F(X) =',F(X))
for i,j in combinations(range(3),2):
 minimum=min(F(update(i,j,2*pi*t/12000,refl))-F(X) for refl in [False,True] for t in range(12000))
 print('Block', (i+1,j+1), 'minimum observed objective difference over rotations and reflections:',minimum)
for s in [-0.5,0,0.5]:
 G=[row[:] for row in G0];G[0][0]+=s
 D=sub(mm(G,tr(X)),mm(X,tr(G)))
 R=sub(G,mm(mm(X,tr(G)),X))
 print('Subgradient parameter',s,'pair skew residuals:',[D[0][1],D[0][2],D[1][2]],'full residual squared:',n2(R))
Omega=[[0,-1,1],[1,0,0],[-1,0,0]]
O2=mm(Omega,Omega)
t=1e-4
R=[[float(i==j)+sin(sqrt(2)*t)/sqrt(2)*Omega[i][j]+(1-cos(sqrt(2)*t))/2*O2[i][j] for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]
Y=mm(R,X)
print('Coupled feasible descent at t=1e-4:',F(Y)-F(X))
print('Coupled path X11:',Y[0][0])
print('Analytic full minimum residual squared is 1/2; each block residual can be zero.')
print('Analytic block proof: F(X_B(V))-F(X) >= <W_BB/2,V-I>+abs((X_B(V))11).')
print('For blocks 12/13 the bound is +/-q*sin(theta)+a*abs(sin(theta)) for rotations and a*abs(sin(theta)) for reflections; for block 23 it is zero.')
PY"

strengths: OBCD’s row updates preserve orthogonality and permit partial-gradient computations. The sufficient-decrease argument under exact block minimization is a useful foundation.
Reducing two-row updates to rotations and reflections provides an attractive approach to separable nonsmooth penalties.
Experiments cover three PCA formulations and ten datasets with several relevant baselines. Table 3 reports substantial nonnegative-PCA objective improvements with negligible nonnegativity violations.
weaknesses: The central stationarity claim is false under the stated assumptions. A counterexample to Theorem 3.8(a) and Lemma 4.4(b) uses a=1/√2, X=[[0,a,a],[a,1/2,-1/2],[a,-1/2,1/2]], W=(a/2)[[0,1,-1],[-1,0,0],[1,0,0]], and F(Y)=〈WX/2−sign(X),Y〉+||Y||₁, with sign(0)=0. Every two-row orthogonal update satisfies F(Y)≥F(X), making X block-2 stationary for Q=0 and any α>0. Nevertheless, min over G∈∂F(X) of ||G−XGᵀX||²_F equals 1/2, so X is not critical. Appendix E.3 incorrectly replaces the existence of a potentially different subgradient for each block with the existence of one subgradient satisfying every block condition.

The stochastic convergence analysis has an independent dependency error. Equations (51)–(52) interchange averaging over Bᵗ and Bᵗ⁺¹ even though the matrix being averaged depends on Xᵗ⁺¹, hence on Bᵗ. Identical marginal sampling distributions do not justify this interchange. Appendix F.4 also applies expectation bounds as pointwise bounds. Consequently, the claimed criticality complexity and KL convergence guarantees are not established.

The main ℓ0-SPCA experiments test a regime with a closed-form solution. Appendix G.2 normalizes ||A||_F=1, implying tr(C)=1 and 0≤tr(XᵀCX)≤1. With every tested λ≥10, any feasible matrix having more than r nonzeros is worse than a matrix with exactly r nonzeros. The optimum therefore consists of signed coordinate vectors selecting the r largest diagonal entries of C. This elementary baseline is missing, and these experiments do not demonstrate performance on a substantive sparsity–variance tradeoff.

The ℓ1-SPCA comparisons initialize OBCD with an identity matrix while initializing every baseline randomly. This confounds algorithmic performance with initialization, particularly under the dominant sparsity penalties used here. Repeated-seed variability, baseline tuning details, reflection/majorizer ablations, and sparsity versus explained-variance results are also missing.

Appendix B contains errors in the claimed exact subproblem solver. The ℓ0 breakpoint list uses xᵢ/yᵢ although zeros of xᵢ+tyᵢ occur at −xᵢ/yᵢ. Discarding pairs with yᵢ=0 is also invalid for ℓ1 regularization because λ|xᵢ|/√(1+t²) still depends on t. The derivation and implementation require verification, since exact global subproblem solutions are essential to the guarantees.
